Halāyudha
(‘one whose weapon is the hala or the plough’)
------------------------------------------
Balarāma, कृष्ण’s elder brother, is said to have equipped himself with two weapons—the hala or the plough and the मुसल or the pestle. Hence he is known as हलायुध and Musalī. See BALARĀMA for details.
Halāyudha is also the name of an author who wrote the well-known Sanskrit dictionary, Abhidhāna-ratna-mālā, also called Halāyudhakoṣa. He lived in the 10th century. Two more works—the Kavirahasya and the Mṛtasañjīvanī are attributed to him.
There was another हलायुध (A.

-1200) too who wrote the work Brāhmaṇasarvasva containing the explanations of the mantras used by a ब्राह्मण in his daily life as also in the performance of the सṁस्कारस् (sacraments). This is a dharmaśāstra work.

Hālāhala
------------------------------------------
When the देवस् (gods) and the दानवस् (demons) were churning the क्षीरसमुद्र or the ocean of milk to get अमृत (ambrosia), one of the by-products was the हालाहल poison. It was so terrific that it started scalding everyone. Then the देवस् and the दानवस् ran to शिव and supplicated to him to save them. शिव gathered it in the palm of his hand and drank it. Since पार्वती, his divine spouse, pressed his throat so that the poison would not go into his stomach and destroy the worlds contained there, it got stuck up there itself, making it dark in colour. Hence शिव got the name ‘Nīlakaṇṭha’, ‘one with a blue or dark neck’ (Bhāgavata 8.7; Rāmāyaṇa, Bālakāṇḍa, 45).
Other names of this poison are: Hālahala, Hāhala, and Hāhāla.
